name: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Buenos Aires
notes: Refined 6 Oct 2026 from published descriptions and the ground's OpenStreetMap outlines, not photographs. MACBA on Avenida San Juan in San Telmo (Vila Sebastián Arquitectos, opened 2012): a 15 m front between party walls, seven floors in exposed concrete, its face one great glazed plane (15 x 12 m) held in a concrete frame over a set-back glass entrance, a slot window above, lower at the back; the brick warehouse of the Museo de Arte Moderno next door to the west and lower houses to the east. The first model put the avenue where the outlines show the block across it: the whole row now stands 27 m further south and 8 m east, on the south side of the avenue, which is drawn at its real width (about 27 m) with the row of older two- to four-storey buildings across it; the lot is shortened to the 36 m the outlines give, and behind it the Autopista 25 de Mayo now runs on its viaduct, as it does. Still guessed: the rear height, the neighbours' heights and colours, the frame's exact proportions, the viaduct's height and piers.
